Velocity fields¶

These routes serve cosmic-flow velocity fields: a three-component vector grid (vx, vy, vz) rather than a scalar cube, read from a single FITS file whose component axis has length 3 (numpy shape (3, nz, ny, nx)). The desktop client fetches the raw vectors and runs streamlines and glyphs locally; derived scalar grids (basins, divergence, field differences) are computed on the backend. See the Velocity-field viewer for the user side.

All binary routes return Content-Type: application/octet-stream with the array as the whole body: little-endian values in C order over (nz, ny, nx), so x varies fastest (the point order of a vtkImageData). Vector grids interleave the three components per point (npts × 3 float32). Shape and metadata travel in X-Visivo-* headers, including X-Visivo-Width (nx), X-Visivo-Height (ny), X-Visivo-Depth (nz), X-Visivo-Components and X-Visivo-Byte-Order: little; float header values are written with Python repr. Unlike the cube routes, X-Visivo-Full-Shape here is ordered nz,ny,nx.

Grid geometry is point-centred on the origin. When the field was opened with a box size box_mpc, the spacing per axis is box_mpc / (n - 1) and the origin is -box_mpc / 2; without it the spacing is 1 (grid units) and the origin is -(n - 1) / 2. The velocity unit is the file’s BUNIT (or km/s (assumed)), the frame its VFRAME (or supergalactic (assumed)).

Errors on the binary routes are text/plain: 404 unknown velocity dataset when the dataset_id is not a velocity field opened in this session, and 500 with the message for a failed computation. None of these routes takes a per-session compute slot.

POST /v1/velocity/open¶

Loads a velocity field, returns its summary and registers it in the session with kind velocity (dataset ids start with vf_).

Request (VelocityOpenRequest): path (server-side path, confined to the backend’s allowed data roots) and box_mpc (default null: physical box size in Mpc; without it the grid uses unit spacing).

{ "path": "/data/cf4/CF4_new_64-z008_velocity.fits", "box_mpc": 1000.0 }

Response (VelocityOpenResponse): valid, error, dataset_id, session_id, and summary with:

Field

Content

shape

[nz, ny, nx]

n_cells

number of grid points

spacing, origin

per axis (x, y, z), Mpc or grid units

unit, frame

as described above

box_known

whether box_mpc was given

warnings

geometry caveats: negative CDELT1..3, a CD/PC matrix with negative determinant (possible mirror image), an assumed frame, no spatial CTYPE

speed_min, speed_max, speed_mean

range and mean of the speed over finite cells

finite_fraction

fraction of cells with a finite speed

Errors: a path outside the allowed data roots (or a hidden path) returns HTTP 200 with valid: false and error: "Velocity file not found."; a missing file, a file that is not a 4-D FITS with a length-3 component axis, and other load failures, return valid: false with the message.

POST /v1/velocity/grid_bin¶

The vector grid for display, optionally block-averaged.

Request (VelocityGridRequest): dataset_id, max_dim (default 128). When max_dim > 0 and the largest grid dimension exceeds it, every component is block-averaged by the integer factor ceil(largest / max_dim) (cropping each axis to a multiple of the factor) and the spacing grows by the same factor. 0 returns the full resolution.

Response: interleaved float32 vectors, nx × ny × nz × 3 values. Headers:

Header

Content

X-Visivo-Width, X-Visivo-Height, X-Visivo-Depth

returned grid size

X-Visivo-Full-Shape

nz,ny,nx before block-averaging

X-Visivo-Downsample-Factor

applied factor (1 when none)

X-Visivo-Components

3

X-Visivo-Spacing, X-Visivo-Origin

x,y,z

X-Visivo-Speed-Min, X-Visivo-Speed-Max

speed range of the returned grid

X-Visivo-Full-Speed-Min, X-Visivo-Full-Speed-Max

speed range at full resolution (block-averaging lowers the maximum)

X-Visivo-Unit, X-Visivo-Frame

velocity unit and frame

POST /v1/velocity/basins_bin¶

Gravitational-basin (watershed) segmentation: the streamline from every grid point is integrated until it converges, and points are labelled by the attractor they reach. direction: 1 gives basins of attraction (superclusters), -1 basins of repulsion (voids).

Request (VelocityBasinsRequest): dataset_id, basin_max_dim (default 64; the field is block-averaged to this largest dimension before segmentation; 0 or negative means 64, and the value is clamped to the range 8 to 96), direction (default 1; any value >= 0 is treated as 1, negative as -1).

Response: an int32 label grid on the coarse basin grid, 0 for unassigned points and 1 to N for basins. Headers: X-Visivo-Width, X-Visivo-Height, X-Visivo-Depth (basin grid size), X-Visivo-Components: 1, X-Visivo-Scalar-Type: int32, X-Visivo-N-Basins. The spacing and origin of the basin grid are not sent; they follow from the block-averaging factor and the field’s geometry.

POST /v1/velocity/density_bin¶

Velocity divergence ∇·v as a density proxy: convergent flow (∇·v < 0) marks overdensities, divergent flow (∇·v > 0) voids. Derivatives are central differences (one-sided at the edges) with the physical spacing, computed in float64. At full resolution, a field whose file size times three exceeds VISIVO_VELOCITY_STREAM_BYTES (default 512 MiB) is processed in z-slabs (VISIVO_VELOCITY_SLAB, default 32) from a memory map, with the same result as the in-memory computation.

Request (VelocityDensityRequest): dataset_id, max_dim (default 0, full resolution; > 0 block-averages first, as in grid_bin).

Response: one float32 scalar per grid point. Headers: X-Visivo-Width, X-Visivo-Height, X-Visivo-Depth, X-Visivo-Components: 1, X-Visivo-Scalar-Type: float32, X-Visivo-Spacing, X-Visivo-Origin, X-Visivo-Div-Min, X-Visivo-Div-Max, X-Visivo-Unit (the velocity unit per Mpc, or per pixel when the box is unknown), X-Visivo-Calibrated: 0, and, only when the box is known, X-Visivo-Density-Factor. The grid is the raw, uncalibrated ∇·v; a linear-theory overdensity is obtained as δ ≈ -∇·v × factor, where the factor is 1 / (f H0) with Planck 2018 values (f = Ωm^0.55, Ωm = 0.3111, H0 = 67.66 km/s/Mpc).

POST /v1/velocity/difference_bin¶

Cell-wise magnitude of the vector difference |v_a - v_b| between two velocity fields (for example two reconstructions, or a reconstruction and a simulation).

Request (VelocityDifferenceRequest): dataset_id_a, dataset_id_b (both velocity fields in this session), max_dim (default 0, full resolution; > 0 block-averages both fields first). Each field uses the box_mpc it was opened with.

{ "dataset_id_a": "vf_0123456789ab", "dataset_id_b": "vf_ba9876543210", "max_dim": 128 }

Response: one float32 scalar per grid point. Headers: X-Visivo-Width, X-Visivo-Height, X-Visivo-Depth, X-Visivo-Components: 1, X-Visivo-Scalar-Type: float32, X-Visivo-Spacing and X-Visivo-Origin (of field A), X-Visivo-Range-Min, X-Visivo-Range-Max, X-Visivo-Unit (field A’s unit), and X-Visivo-Warnings when there is anything to report: the two fields’ own geometry warnings, different box sizes, different units or different frames, joined with ; (Latin-1, single line).

Errors: 404 (text/plain) when either id is not a velocity field in the session, 422 (text/plain) when the two grids have different shapes, 500 for other failures.

POST /v1/velocity/subgrid_bin¶

A full-resolution region of the field, read through a memory map so only the region is loaded.

Request (VelocitySubgridRequest): dataset_id, x0, x1, y0, y1, z0, z1 (full-resolution grid indices). The end index is exclusive here, unlike the inclusive cube routes. Each start is clamped to [0, n - 1] and each end to [start + 1, n], so the region is never empty.

{ "dataset_id": "vf_0123456789ab", "x0": 96, "x1": 160, "y0": 96, "y1": 160, "z0": 96, "z1": 160 }

Response: interleaved float32 vectors of the region. Headers: X-Visivo-Width, X-Visivo-Height, X-Visivo-Depth (region size), X-Visivo-Components: 3, X-Visivo-Roi-X0, X-Visivo-Roi-Y0, X-Visivo-Roi-Z0 (clamped start indices, to place the region in the full grid), X-Visivo-Full-Shape (nz,ny,nx), X-Visivo-Speed-Min, X-Visivo-Speed-Max. Spacing, origin, unit and frame are not sent; the client places the region from the start indices and the full grid’s geometry.
